account:
Today I kept office hours and came to the mill for my ten o'clock grain inspection. Several townsfolk near the mill and bakery have repeated reports of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 11 named the baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as having been there. This is unusual news, but I have no concrete description of the change, no time for it, and no confirmation that these people witnessed it themselves. I asked for specifics and asked neighbour directly; so far I have heard only neighbour's greeting and reminder of our fifteen hundred tea, not an explanation. Freight has also been nearby, but I could not make out his recent words.

There are lanterns around the bakery. Yesterday neighbour described its cheerful lights as simply to brighten the building. The builder has arranged a formally approved great hall lighting inspection for eighteen hundred today; secretary said it concerns newly installed lanterns and their coverage, with no particular problem reported. Neighbour offered to accompany me there after our regular dockside tea. Those arrangements might be entirely routine. I do not yet have evidence connecting the lighting inspection to the reported bridge or port change.

My tentative understanding is that some discussion involving river access or trade has occurred at the bakery among baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour. Its purpose remains unknown; I should not mistake repeated vague reports for a verified plan. I want a direct explanation while keeping today's appointments: mill now, home at noon, office at thirteen, tea at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, hall inspection at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
